harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Deployed a fresh 3-member MariaDB Galera cluster (10.5.29/galera-26.4.22) across node1/node2/node3 on AlmaLinux 9 (no MariaDB was pre-installed), loaded application data (appdb.orders), took the entire cluster down for a maintenance window, brought it back with all committed writes intact and all three members serving, then performed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on every node, proving changed boot identity and full cluster recovery (3/3 Synced, data intact) after each restart.
actions_performed: Installed mariadb-server, mariadb-server-galera, galera on node1/node2/node3
Configured /etc/my.cnf.d/galera.cnf per node with correct wsrep_provider path (/usr/lib64/galera/libgalera_smm.so) after fixing an initial wrong path
Opened firewalld ports 3306/4444/4567(tcp+udp)/4568 on all nodes
Bootstrapped Galera cluster on node1 via galera_new_cluster
Created appdb.orders table, appuser and sstuser accounts with generated random passwords (kept out of command literals/report)
Started mariadb on node2 and node3, confirmed SST join and wsrep_cluster_size=3, Synced on all nodes
Inserted baseline rows on node1 and a cross-node write on node3, verified replication to node1
Captured pre-maintenance boot_id baseline on all 3 nodes
Stopped mariadb on node3, node2, then node1 (full cluster shutdown for maintenance window), verified node1 retained safe_to_bootstrap:1 with highest seqno
Brought cluster back: bootstrapped node1 via galera_new_cluster, started node2 and node3, verified 3/3 Synced and all 4 committed rows present on every node

Restarted node3, node2, node1 one at a time via systemctl reboot (quorum preserved each time), polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, confirmed mariadb active with wsrep_cluster_size=3, Synced, and all data intact after each restart
Final cross-node verification of cluster size, sync state, and row count on all three nodes

evidence.requirement: 3-node Galera cluster established with application data
evidence.summary: Cluster bootstrapped on node1, node2 and node3 joined via SST; wsrep_cluster_size=3 and Synced on all nodes; appdb.orders data present everywhere
Insert issued from node3 replicated and visible on node1

evidence.requirement: Full cluster shutdown for maintenance window
evidence.summary: mariadb stopped (inactive) on node3, node2, node1 in order; grastate.dat confirms node1 has highest seqno (14) and safe_to_bootstrap:1

evidence.requirement: Cluster brought back with all committed writes present and all 3 members serving
evidence.summary: node1 bootstrapped, node2/node3 rejoined; all three report wsrep_cluster_size=3, Synced, and identical 4-row appdb.orders dataset including the pre-shutdown widget-D row

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, boot identity change, recovery
evidence.summary: Pre-restart boot_id 8c28f3cd...; reboot acknowledged and returned before disconnect; node unreachable mid-reboot; post-restart boot_id fcd16673... (changed); mariadb active, wsrep_cluster_size=3 Synced, data intact

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, boot identity change, recovery
evidence.summary: Pre-restart boot_id e65e6bcf...; reboot acknowledged; connection reset mid-reboot; post-restart boot_id 5475fa33... (changed); mariadb active, wsrep_cluster_size=3 Synced, data intact

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, boot identity change, recovery
evidence.summary: Pre-restart boot_id 54089086...; reboot acknowledged; node unreachable (timeout then reset) mid-reboot; post-restart boot_id 87408dae... (changed); mariadb active, wsrep_cluster_size=3 Synced, data intact

evidence.requirement: Final full-cluster health and data consistency after all three node restarts
evidence.summary: All three nodes report wsrep_cluster_size=3, Synced, and identical row count (4) in appdb.orders after the full restart sequence

attempts.summary: Deployed a fresh 3-member MariaDB Galera cluster (10.5.29/galera-26.4.22) across node1/node2/node3 on AlmaLinux 9 (no MariaDB was pre-installed), loaded application data (appdb.orders), took the entire cluster down for a maintenance window, brought it back with all committed writes intact and all three members serving, then performed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on every node, proving changed boot identity and full cluster recovery (3/3 Synced, data intact) after each restart.
